title: Oath and Choir
premise: Emrys Brightwater, a temple scribe bound by debt to the Choir of Saint Vess, copies forbidden texts to buy his freedom—until he finds tonight's date in a century-old prophecy naming him the thief who will steal back a soul from the Hollow Court beneath Thornfell. The soul belongs to Wren, a smuggler girl who sold it to save her brother, and the Court's regent will stop at nothing to keep it. Hunted by his own temple masters, who would rather fulfill the prophecy's darker second half—sealing the mountain forever with Wren inside—Emrys gathers a found family of outcasts to breach the Court. In the end, Emrys learns loyalty means telling hard truths: he breaks his oath to the Choir, offers his own name in trade for Wren's soul, and discovers that names freely given are the one currency power cannot corrupt.
about_author: Mara Vane is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing medieval choir manuscripts before turning to fantasy. She writes stories about people trapped by institutions, and lives in a drafty house full of unlabeled maps.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV. A night of copying contraband maps for smugglers establishes his double life: obedient scribe by day, invisible broker by night. When he transcribes an old prophecy and finds tomorrow's date beside his own name, his careful anonymity shatters. Emotional beat: dread disguised as routine—the moment invisibility stops being safety.

chapters.title: What Wren Sold
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. The smuggler Emrys knows only as a client arrives bleeding, having learned her brother's life was bought with her soul, now held by the Hollow Court beneath Thornfell. She begs Emrys to find a way down. He refuses—but copies her name into his private ledger anyway. Emotional beat: guilt kindling into resolve.

chapters.title: The Choir's Second Verse
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV. Summoned before Archcantor Halden, Emrys discovers the temple has known of the prophecy for years—and intends to fulfill its second clause: sealing the mountain with the stolen soul inside, buying the Choir another century of influence. Halden offers Emrys freedom in exchange for silence. Emotional beat: the seduction of complicity.

chapters.title: A Company of the Unwanted
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV rotation through brief vignettes. Emrys assembles allies: Brannoc, a disgraced court musician who knows the Court's songs; Sister Ivet, a heretic nun; and Wren herself, against his better judgment. Each joins for their own wound. Emotional beat: wary strangers becoming the skeleton of a family.

chapters.title: Down the Smuggler's Road
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV. The descent through Thornfell's abandoned mine-roads, guided by Emrys's secret knowledge, while temple hunters close behind. Wren catches him lying about the route's dangers and calls him a coward who hides truth inside kindness. Emotional beat: first real fracture—and first honest words between them.

chapters.title: The Singing Gate
chapters.summary: Brannoc, POV. The party reaches the Court's gate, which opens only to a song sung without deceit. Brannoc must perform a confession-song exposing his own disgrace, nearly collapsing under it. The gate opens; something on the other side opens its eyes. Emotional beat: vulnerability as literal key.

chapters.title: Court of Borrowed Names
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. Inside the Hollow Court, souls are kept as ledger entries and the regent wears the faces of those who traded with him. Wren confronts the contract bearing her signature and learns the regent wants not her soul but Emrys's name—the prophecy's true prize. Emotional beat: horror at how cheaply she once valued herself.

chapters.title: Halden's Hand
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV. The temple hunters arrive—not to rescue but to complete the sealing, with Halden offering the regent the Choir's cooperation if Wren is left behind. Betrayed by his institution, Emrys chooses openly at last, burning his debt-ledger before them all. Emotional beat: liberation through ruin.

chapters.title: The Price of a Name
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV. Climax. To void Wren's contract, Emrys offers the regent his true name—freely given, uncoerced—which no power can hold, because a gift cannot be owned. The Court's ledgers unravel as the regent tries to claim what was never sold. Halden is sealed instead by his own greed. Emotional beat: sacrifice that costs everything and buys truth.

chapters.title: Choir of the Free
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Rising from the mountain, the survivors find the prophecy's final line blank—written for whoever chose to act. Wren, soul restored, reunites with her brother; Ivet founds a new order; Brannoc sings again. Emrys, nameless but known, takes up a new ledger with one entry: debts forgiven. Emotional beat: quiet joy—family chosen, oaths rewritten.
